Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot (Tomato)
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A serious bacterial disease causing leaf spots, defoliation, and fruit lesions.
symptoms: Spots turn dark brown to black
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.pestDetails: Bacterial spread via splashing water or insects.

treatment.fertilizer: Maintain balanced nutrition, avoid excessive nitrogen.
treatment.applicationMethod: Foliar spray, covering both sides of leaves.
treatment.timeline: Apply every 7-10 days upon symptom onset.
treatment.precautions: Avoid spraying during peak sun. Wear protective gear.

prevention: Remove and destroy infected plant debris

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight (Tomato)
Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease causing rapid defoliation and reduced yields.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target spots)
Tomato___Early_blight.pestDetails: Fungal spores spread by wind and water.

treatment.fertilizer: Potassium rich fertilizers to strengthen cell walls.
treatment.precautions: Do not harvest immediately after spraying.

prevention: Water at the base of the plant

Potato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight (Potato)
Potato___Late_blight.description: The devastating disease that caused the Irish Potato Famine, attacking both leaves and tubers.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark green/black spots on leaves
White fungal growth on undersides in wet weather

treatment.precautions: Requires immediate action; can destroy crop in days.

healthy.name: Healthy Plant
healthy.description: Your plant appears to be healthy with no visible signs of major diseases.

treatment.organicAlternatives: Routine neem oil spray for prevention.

prevention: Ensure proper sunlight and air circulation
